# AntiMage v0.1.4

_Released: 2026-09-11_

## Highlights

- Added the production native OpenVPN inbound runtime for Linux binary nodes.
- The node agent now generates and manages OpenVPN server/runtime files and the OpenVPN process lifecycle.
- OpenVPN client TCP and UDP traffic is routed through Linux TPROXY into the node's Xray transparent inbound so configured Xray routing and outbounds are applied.
- Added native OpenVPN authentication, user status and expiry policy enforcement, traffic/quota enforcement with live cutoff, device-limit enforcement, session start/seen/stop callbacks, and persisted usage accounting with acknowledgement handling.
- Added graceful cleanup for OpenVPN processes and TPROXY routing state.
- Added tests covering the native OpenVPN runtime and controller integration.

## Behavior changes

- The native OpenVPN runtime requires the `openvpn` executable to be installed and available on the Linux node `PATH`.
- The OpenVPN/TPROXY native runtime is Linux-specific.
- The current transparent path proxies TCP and UDP traffic through Xray. ICMP/ping is not proxied through Xray.
- OpenVPN can listen on any available configured port; any public relay or forwarding layer must use the same protocol and port.

## Upgrade notes

- Existing installations can install or update the node binary to `v0.1.4` after the release assets are published.
- When exposing OpenVPN through an L3 relay or tunnel, point the client at the public relay endpoint and forward the configured OpenVPN TCP/UDP port to the AntiMage node.
- Ensure firewall rules allow the selected OpenVPN port and that the node can create the required TUN, policy-routing, and TPROXY state.

## Checksums

Checksums are published with the GitHub release assets.
